summary: Enforced model pin suppressed by fallback-throttle preemption during canary window, causing mixed-model responses
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightAssist reported intermittent mixed-model outputs despite having an explicit tenant model pin configured. Impact: a subset (~4%) of requests during the canary window returned responses generated by a compat/legacy variant instead of the pinned model, causing degraded answer quality and downstream QA alerts. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod(us-east), pinned via tenant config to redwood-7b-v1.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Trigger canary rollout for redwood-7b-v1 -> redwood-7b-v2 in same region with 10% weight
3) Simulate load spike with concurrent prefix-heavy streams (50 RPS sustained for 10m)
4) Observe router logs and serving runtime traces for requests that should honor tenant pin
logs: edge-proxy trace: req=1a7c3f7e tenant=brightassist route=chat model_hint=redwood-7b-v1 fallback_reason=throttle_preemptor selected_model=redwood-1.5b-v2
orchestrator log snippet: 2026-03-11T15:42:08Z WARN fallback-controller: preemptive-throttle triggered for slice 10; suppressed explicit_pin=true for cohort 'tenant-42' to preserve SLOs
serving-runtime: request_id=1a7c3f7e latency=1200ms kvcache_hits=0 selected_variant=compat-v1 (fallback path)
comments: 2026-03-11 16:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer reported unexpected answer changes at ~15:40 UTC during canary. Provided request IDs and example outputs. They see mixed outputs for some user sessions despite explicit pin.

2026-03-11 16:22 - SRE (Liam Chen): Reproduced similar trace in prod; fallback-controller emitted preemptive-throttle event and set decision to allow degraded variant for a short window. Investigating why explicit pin was not honored.

2026-03-11 17:04 - Eng (Priya Sundar): Hypothesis: fallback-controller has a higher priority rule for latency mitigation that can preempt per-tenant pins when aggregate slot pressure exceeds a threshold. Need to confirm the rule evaluation order and recent config changes.

2026-03-11 19:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (rollback canary and set strict capacity cap). Asking for ETA on fix and whether billing will be adjusted for impacted requests.

2026-03-12 09:18 - Eng (Liam Chen): Identified change in controller ordering deployed 2026-03-10 (PR #872) that introduced 'preemptive-throttle' as a higher-priority branch. Preparing a rollback of that behavioral change for emergency patch.

2026-03-14 11:10 - Eng (Liam Chen): Hotfix deployed to route-controller that enforces tenant pin precedence over preemptive fallback except under Sev0 global overload. Monitoring telemetry; customer confirmed no mixed-model responses in last 6 hours. Drafting follow-up change to add metrics and a toggle.
2026-03-14 11:45 - Customer (BrightAssist - T. Moreno): Confirmed improved behavior and restored quality. Asked for postmortem and timeline for full fix.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Not an auth or cookie issue. All affected requests had valid pin metadata attached at the ingress layer.

Correlated events: A canary rollout in the same region created a transient slot pressure pattern; fallback-controller responded by enabling preemptive-throttle to maintain P95 latency SLOs across tenants.

Root cause hypothesis: Route-controller policy evaluation order was changed in PR #872; preemptive-throttle branch was assigned a precedence above explicit tenant pin checks, allowing it to override pins during short overload windows.
Telemetry: During the incident window (15:38 - 15:51 UTC) fallback-controller logged 1,340 preemptive events; of those ~52 had explicit_pin=true and were forced to compat-variant selection.
Partial repro: Replayed the same traffic profile against staging with the new policy and reproduced pin suppression consistently when queue depth > 800 and prewarm cache miss ratio > 60%.

Edge-case note: Requests that were streaming with prefix > 1024 tokens disproportionately hit the fallback path due to increased per-token cost estimation and conservative slot accounting in the throttle algorithm.
resolution: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-11 20:10 UTC): Rolled back policy precedence change from PR #872 in the route-controller and toggled off preemptive-throttle for non-global overload conditions. Customer canary rolled back at their request to stop quality variance.

Hotfix (2026-03-14 11:05 UTC): Deployed patch that enforces explicit tenant pin precedence in policy evaluator. Added safety check to allow preemptive-throttle only when global cluster overload is detected (Sev0).
- ENG-8471: Add telemetry and dashboards for 'pin-suppressed-by-fallback' events (owner: Priya Sundar).
- OPS-5490: Add a canary guard that isolates pinned-tenants from preemptive-throttle decisions unless explicitly opted-in (owner: Liam Chen).
- CS to offer credit: recommend finance review for impacted token billing with BrightAssist (owner: Maya Patel).
- Postmortem: Schedule postmortem and publish to Confluence with timeline and corrective steps (owner: SRE lead).
Customer status: BrightAssist confirmed behavior stable as of 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC; team requested formal postmortem and follow-up on billing impact.
